claims: Composite DTM represents terrain after surface-object removal
Composite DTM is a raster elevation model
The 1m composite covers about 99 percent of England
Composite production merges time-stamped and national programme surveys
Repeat coverage prefers the newest best-resolution survey
Resampled inputs use bilinear interpolation
Coverage metadata identifies the contributing survey
Time-stamped archives preserve survey-specific dates
Raster downloads use GeoTIFF
Downloads are packaged in 5km tiles
Tiles align to the OS National Grid
Coverage and survey metadata are separately available
WMS provides summarised elevation presentation
WCS provides elevation coverage values
Persistent endpoints remove annual year suffixes
First-return and last-return products have distinct endpoints
Horizontal CRS is EPSG:27700
Elevations are supplied in metres
Elevations reference Ordnance Datum Newlyn
Composite transformation uses OSTN15 and OSGM15 lineage
Individual LIDAR surveys target plus or minus 15cm RMSE
Ground-truth points target plus or minus 3cm RMSE
Ground-truth comparison evaluates RMSE and standard deviation
Ground-truth surveys have age limits for reuse
DSM includes buildings vegetation and vehicles
DTM removes surface objects through algorithms and manual editing
First-return DSM uses the first or only laser return
Point-cloud ground classification may differ from final edited DTM
A dataset contract does not prove coverage at TQ2892
Exact filtered metadata is required for candidate binding
Exact WCS cell values are required for numeric promotion
Absent candidate coverage or values remain blocked
